scope: USPSTF 2021 recommendation statement on annual low-dose CT screening for lung cancer, including who to screen and when to stop.

keyRecommendations.text: Screen annually with LDCT adults aged 50 to 80 years with a 20 pack-year history who currently smoke or quit within the past 15 years.
Stop screening once a person has not smoked for 15 years or develops a health problem that substantially limits life expectancy or the ability or willingness to have curative lung surgery.

clinicalBottomLine: Offer annual LDCT to adults 50–80 with at least 20 pack-years who still smoke or quit within 15 years, and stop after 15 smoke-free years or when curative surgery is no longer realistic.
notableCaveats: The page text used does not include the words Grade B in the extracted recommendation paragraph, so the grade letter is not taught here. NLST is a separate topic.

source.title: Lung Cancer: Screening. U.S. Preventive Services Task Force recommendation.
